Risk Management Plan

Introduction
This document was developed for the Facility located at 11704 Road 120, GFP Ethanol LLC dba Calgren Renewable Fuels (Calgren), Pixley, CA 93256 to fulfill criteria of the RMP standard, as required by Section 112(r) of the Clean Air Act and regulated by 40 CFR, Part 68.

Under the accidental release provisions of the Clean Air Act, regulated sources are required to conduct hazard assessments, review off-site consequence analyses and develop a risk management plan. The hazard assessment discusses off-site consequences for a Worst Case Scenario (WCS) and Alternative Release Scenario (ARS) of the regulated substances(s) at this Facility. From the subsequent analyses of the scenario(s), accident prevention programs will be reviewed, revised, and implemented.

Emergency response programs will also be reviewed/enhanced in an effort to minimize the impact of the potential consequences resulting from an accidental release of regulated substances in the covered process.

There are two primary purposes of the development of the Section 112(r) regulations, paraphrasing the intents of the U.S. Congress and EPA:

1. To encourage sources to reduce the probability and severity of accidental releases
having the potential to cause harm to the public and the environment.
2. To stimulate a dialogue between industry and the public to improve accident prevention
and emergency response.

The RMP standard applies to facilities that store greater than a threshold quantity of a regulated substance in a process at any one time. The facility has a process involving flammables (denaturant or natural gasoline) above the threshold quantity (TQ) of 10,000 pounds, listed in 40 CFR, Section 68.115. Therefore, EPA's RMP applies. Flammables (denaturant) is the only substance in the Facility's current chemical usage inventory, which would be present in quantities above the TQ limits set by the EPA, triggering the requirement for submitting this RMP.

Accidental Releas

e Prevention and Emergency Response Policies
It is this Facility's intent to uphold industry standards in the operation of the Facility and it is our policy to adhere to all applicable federal, state, and local laws. The facility has been designed and constructed to be a state-of-the-art facility employing numerous release identification and prevention measures. If a minor incident were to occur, in-house staff are trained and equipped to perform isolation measures and secure leaking systems. If the incident escalates, Calgren would immediately initiate the 911 system and the Tulare County Fire Department would respond to the emergency at the Facility. The Tulare County Fire Department also has mutual aid agreements with other fire departments and local HAZMAT Teams for additional emergency support should the need arise.

Stationary Source and Regulated Substances Handled
The primary purpose of the flammables (denaturant) at this Facility is the production of fuel grade ethanol. Physical access by non-employees to the flammables is somewhat restricted by the general site fencing, security cameras, and chemical contractor protocols/procedures and by the employees being on-site 24 hours and 365 days per year. Within the Facility, the bulk denaturant tank is in the tank farm on the north end of the facility.

Worst-Case Release Scenario and the Alternative Release Scenarios
In accordance with 40 CFR Part 60 Section 112r (the RMP regulations), an off-site consequence analysis must be conducted and evaluated for each chemical (toxic and/or flammable) above the regulated threshold quantity. The EPA's RMP modeling program, RMP Comp, was utilized for this analysis.

Worst Case: Release of the entire contents of the tank would be 472,795 pounds. For WCS, according to EPA's RMP modeling program, RMP Comp, the distance to flammable endpoint is 0.6 miles. The facility is located in a rural setting, with an estimated population of 67 people residing within the 0.6 mile radius. T

he data was obtained on Circular Area Profiles (CAPs) which uses 2020 United States Census Data.

Alternate Case: This is a more likely release scenario for the substance under normal operation conditions. A release of 4358 lbs/minute of denaturant for 10 minutes results in a distance to a toxic endpoint of 0.1 miles. This distance will not reach any person based on Circular Area Profiles (CAPs) which uses 2020 United States Census Data.

General Accidental Release Prevention Program and the Specific Prevention Steps
This Facility complies with EPA's Accidental Release Prevention Rule and with all applicable state codes and regulations. Calgren takes a systematic, proactive approach to evaluating chemical processes.

Using this approach, the design, technology, operation and maintenance activities, emergency preparedness plans, training, process changes and other elements that affect the covered processes are all considered. By conducting thorough evaluations, accidental releases are prevented, and the consequences of releases are minimized.

Through fulfilling the required elements of the RMP standard, Calgren intends to prevent releases of hazardous substances and minimize the impacts of accidental releases into locations that could expose employees, the community or the environment to serious hazards. The Calgren program addresses each of the key features of a successful release "Prevention Program" including:
Maintaining PSI: Calgren maintains up-to-date technical information about safe operating limits of the components and the associated hazards of the chemicals involved.

Conducting PHA: Calgren performs technical analyses of the plant's processes to anticipate what might go wrong and recommend approaches to minimize the possibilities and effects of such occurrences.

Standard Operating Procedures (SOP): Calgren has written technical and administrative procedures used to operate the plant safely.

Training: Calgren provides employees with information necessar

y to ensure safe operation.

Mechanical Integrity (MI): Calgren conducts maintenance of the process equipment on an ongoing basis.

Management of Change (MOC): Calgren analyzes changes in process equipment, procedures and personnel to understand the impact of those changes in the safe operation of our plant.

PSSR: Calgren requires necessary elements for operating a safe process prior to introducing the hazardous chemical into a "new" or modified system.

Compliance Audits: Calgren conducts periodic evaluation and updating of the process operation so that RMP elements are being applied properly.

Incident Investigation: Calgren has procedures for investigating the causes of near miss or accidental releases and developing measures to prevent future similar occurrences.

Employee Participation: Calgren has a philosophy and approach of incorporating the knowledge and experience of our employees from all facets of operation regarding the covered processes.

Contractors: Calgren upholds policies and procedures for safe work practices of contractors on the Facility and a systematic approach of communicating hazards inherent to the covered processes which the contractor may be working on or near Calgren employees are committed to the standards inherent in the RMP regulation.

Calgren has established specific accountabilities and controls that incorporate high standards for accident prevention. Calgren has also developed a risk management system which identifies specific job positions and responsibilities to facilitate proper management and implementation of this RMP.

There have been no accidental releases of hazardous chemicals in the past five years, which have resulted in off-site consequences such as personal injury, death, or response/restoration type activities.

Emergency Response Program
Calgren relies on trained, in-house staff and on-site equipment of for initial response to incidental spills and releases (if safe to do so), and will acquire backup support from t

he Tulare County Fire Department and HAZMAT representatives as needed.
Calgren will discuss the content and intent of this program with the CDF Fire Department.

Planned Changes to Improve Safety
Besides the identified recommendations from the PHA's, Calgren intends to incorporate updated maintenance and inspection procedures of the process equipment and operator training to facilitate the mechanical integrity and the safe operation of this system. Calgren also plans on conducting table-top drills with the local emergency agency in order to be better prepared for possible accident/release scenarios.

Applicability
The Facility has a process involving quantities of flammables (denaturant) above the threshold quantity (TQ) of 10,000 pounds, listed in 40 CFR, Section 68.115. Therefore, EPA's RMP applies. Denaturant is the only substances in the Facility's current chemical usage inventory, which would be present in quantities above the TQ limits set by the EPA, triggering the requirement for submitting this RMP.

Program Level Determination
Determining which program level the Facility is subject to within the RMP Guidelines requires development of a WCS and/or Off-site Consequence Analysis (OCA) and a review of the Facility's accident history with respect to the covered process for the previous five years.

Calgren is not eligible for Program 1 because the distance to hazardous endpoint derived in the WCS includes public receptors. Also, Calgrens process involving flammables (denaturant) is subject to OSHA's PSM Program requirements. Therefore, Calgren has a "Program 3" process.

Hazard Assessment Elements
The next step for RMP development is to conduct the hazard assessment. The essential elements of this assessment are as follows:
Off-site consequence analysis parameters (discussed in worst-case and alternative release scenarios) WCS analysis (completed in subsequent section of this document) ARS analysis (one for each hazardous chemical, completed in subsequent sect

ion of this document).

 Defining off-site impacts on population. Population estimates and identification of major public receptors (i.e., schools, hospitals, other businesses, public roads) Defining off-site impacts on the environment. Identification of any national or state parks, federal wilderness areas, officially designated wildlife refuges, etc.

Review and update. Calgren will review and update this RMP at least once every five years as required by the standard. Also, if changes to the process occur which might reasonably be expected to alter the distance to endpoint calculations, the plan will be reviewed and changes implemented within six months of such alterations. 

Documentation. Calgren will maintain derived records and subsequent documents generated as a result of this analysis Calgren will maintain a five-year accident history of all accidental releases from the covered process which result in deaths, injuries, or significant property damage on-site, or known off-site deaths, injuries, evacuation, sheltering in place, property damage, or environmental damage. Facility has had no incidents in the last five years resulting in any reportable occurrences as described by Section 68.42.

Worst Case Scenario Analysis
Using the specified conditions set forth in the RMP Guidance EPA 550-B-98-110 and the EPA's modeling program, RMP Comp, the distance to endpoint for denaturant is 0.6 miles.
Using 2020 Census Data, the estimated population within this radius is 67 people.

Alternative Release Scenario (ARS) Analysis
An ARS is required for each hazardous chemical held at the Facility above the TQ specified in Section 68.115 for facilities having Program 3 processes. This includes completing an ARS for the chemical used in the WCS, as well as an ARS for each additional toxic chemical present in quantities above the TQ. The ARS's are to be developed with the additional criteria that they must be: 1) more likely to occur than the WCS and 2) the distance to endpoint

is greater than the distance to the nearest public receptor, if such a scenario exists. In the ARS, some of the specified weather conditions are changed with respect to the WCS and one is permitted to consider active mitigation systems, which would limit the release of the chemical.

Using the specified conditions set forth in exhibit 4-12 and 4-20 of the RMP Guidance EPA 550-B-98- 010 and the EPA's modeling program, RMP Comp, the distance to the endpoint for denaturant is 0.1 miles. Modeling results define the distance to endpoint and population estimates of the affected area.

Prevention Program
Calgren has been determined to be a Program 3 facility.

Process safety information
Process hazard analysis
Operating procedures
Training

Process Safety Information

Calgren has developed and maintains written information relating to the denaturant system. It is the EH&S Coordinator responsibility to update and maintain this information. Future PHA teams will use this information during the required periodic compliance audits of this RMP. 

Hazard Review
PHAs were conducted using the HAZOP methodology for identifying potential hazardous consequences, causes, safeguards and hazard mitigation actions. This assessment was facilitated by PROtect, LLC. 

Operating Procedures
Calgren has developed SOPs for its systems using hazardous chemicals. Operating procedures include operating limits, consequences of process deviation and steps to correct or avoid deviations. Safety and health considerations have been included in these procedures. Safety systems and their functions have also been identified. 
The Production Manager will review the operating procedures annually so that the procedures reflect the current operating practices. The Production Manager will also review the following safety practices and

polices:
Respiratory protection
Lockout/tagout
Confined space entry
Opening process equipment or piping
Control entrance into a facility by maintenance contractor, vendor, or other support
Personnel 

Safety program / hazard communication / employee right-to-know program Training
Calgren is committed to establishing the safest possible environment for its employees and the community surrounding its operations. Calgren has established a comprehensive training program to meet the requirements under both the EPA's RMP Standard and OSHA's PSM Standard. 

Calgren has established initial and refresher training modules for several safety programs. The Facility's operators and maintenance personnel are provided training on an annual basis. The EH&S Manager of the plant will coordinate and document the provided safety training.

Contractors (if used at all) are provided training based on the work they conduct on or adjacent to the denaturant system. Their employers are responsible for providing OSHA-mandated training. Calgren will provide the appropriate training to contractors required by the RMP and PSM Standards as they pertain to the denaturant system.

Mechanical Integrity
The maintenance programs and schedules are in-place and periodically reviewed to facilitate proper "ongoing" mechanical integrity. The basic contents of these programs are found in previous sections of this manual.

This section applies to the following process equipment:
1. Pressure vessels and storage tanks
2. Piping systems (including piping components such as valves)
3. Relief and vent systems and devices
4. Emergency shutdown systems
5. Controls (including monitoring devices, and alarms)

Written procedures to maintain the ongoing integrity of process equipment have been implemented. The written procedures include a list of pressure vessels, storage tanks, process piping, relief and vent systems, fire system components, emergency shutdown systems, alarms, pumps and peripheral equipment. Each empl

oyee involved in maintaining the ongoing integrity of process equipment will be trained in an overview of those processes and their hazards and in the procedures applicable to the employee's job tasks to assure that the employee can perform the job tasks in a safe manner.

Inspections and tests performed on process equipment follow recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices. Each inspection and test that is performed on process equipment is documented. Deficiencies in equipment that are outside acceptable limits will be corrected in a safe and timely manner before further use to assure safe operation.

In the construction of new facilities and changes in current equipment, assurance will be made by the Plant Manager that equipment, as it is fabricated, is suitable for the process application for which it will be used. Appropriate checks and inspections will be performed so that the equipment is installed properly and consistent with design specifications and the manufacturer's instructions. Maintenance materials, spare parts and equipment will be suitable for the process application for which they will be used. These issues will be properly addressed as defined by the MOC procedures.

Field equipment installation work will be inspected for use of proper materials and procedures to verify that qualified craft workers do the job.
The use of appropriate gaskets, packing, bolts, valves, lubricants and welding rods will be verified in the field. Also, procedures for installing safety devices will be verified in the field, such as the torque on the bolts on rupture disc installations, uniform torque on flange bolts and proper installation of pump seals.

Management of Change (MOC)
MOC procedures for the covered process are defined in Management of Change MOC section of the PSM program manual. Calgren has developed a procedure to manage process changes. MOC procedures include changes in chemical, operating procedures, or system components. The Plant Manag

er, Production Manager and the Maintenance Manager shall approve of any changes before they are implemented. It is the Plant Manager's responsibility to verify that identified items on the checklist requiring action are completed. All requirements will be addressed prior to the changes to any process, chemical, operating procedures, or system component modifications.

Pre-Start-up Safety Review (PSSR)
Procedures for conducting PSSRs are given in PSM Section of this manual. Calgren will conduct a PSSR prior to a new process startup or when changes are made other than replacement of kind to the existing systems. The plant management staff will determine if a process change qualifies as a "modification" or "replacement of kind". Modifications to the process will require a pre-startup review before any startup can occur.

Compliance Audits
Calgren will evaluate and certify compliance of RMP regulations at least every three years, to verify that the procedures and practices developed under the rule are still adequate and are being followed. The compliance audit will be conducted by at least one person knowledgeable in RMP and/or the process. Calgren will promptly determine and document an appropriate response to each of the findings of the compliance audit and document that deficiencies have been corrected. Calgren will retain the two most recent compliance audit reports on-site. This requirement does not apply to any compliance audit report that is more than five years old.

Incident Investigation
Calgren will investigate each incident (or near miss) which resulted in, or could reasonably have resulted in, a catastrophic release of a hazardous chemical. An incident investigation will be initiated as promptly as possible, but not later than 24 hours following the incident.
The EH&S Coordinator will use the Incident Report form along with the review of Management to summarize and report any findings from the incident investigation and follow investigation items outlined o

n the incident report.

Calgren will promptly address and resolve the investigation findings and recommendations. Resolutions and corrective actions will be documented and maintained as part of the RMP. The findings will be reviewed with affected personnel. Investigation summaries will be retained for five years.
Employee Participation
Calgren believes firmly in, and is committed to, employee participation in the PSM/RMP development and implementation. Involvement will lead to a better understanding by all of the hazards, operating procedures, safety systems, start-up procedures, shutdown procedures, training, contractor involvement, maintenance, emergency planning and emergency response necessary to implement a full and complete program Employees (or an employee representative) will be directly involved in developing each of the following PSM / RMP elements:
Process hazard analysis
Process hazard analysis revalidation
Operating procedures
Process maintenance procedures
Management of change procedures
Incident investigation procedures
Emergency planning and response procedures

Affected employees will be asked for suggestions and remarks pertaining to the PSM/RMP programs during many of the other related safety training courses (i.e., hazard communication (employee right-to-know), emergency response plans, lockout/tagout, hot work program, etc.). The suggestions will then be acted on and the results communicated to the employees.
 
Upon request, Calgren provides employees (or their representatives) access to elements of the PSM/RMP Programs. The Plant Manager or Production Manager will keep a copy of this program for employee access.

Contractors
Calgren is concerned with the safety and welfare of their employees. Calgren wants to be consistent in contract administration involving the safety responsibilities of contractors.

The contractor's implementation of their own safety program is an important part of Calgren's safety program. Each contractor working on or nea

r the covered process must comply with federal and state occupational safety and health regulations. 

Risk Management Plan Submittal
The EPA requires submittal of an abbreviated version (Plan) of the original RMP to USEPA by June 21,1999, or on the date the Facility stores any regulated substance above the applicable threshold quantity; and the rule requires five-year resubmittals to update revisions on the original Plan within five years after the first implementation of the Facility's RMP.

The Plan includes the executive summary of this document, a signed certification statement regarding the content and accuracy of the RMP and specific data elements outlined by the EPA in their RMP
Emergency Response
GFP Ethanol LLC dba Calgren Renewable Fuels will use local and state emergency responders to respond to releases. The emergency response team's actions and employee evacuation will aid in the prevention of a catastrophic event from occurring. The responding groups, Tulare County Fire Department and Hazardous Materials Response (HAZMAT) Teams are comprised of area fire department personnel trained in HAZMAT responses. These teams are the designated emergency responders to leaks, spills, fires and releases of significant hazardous materials at Calgren Facility. The local/state regional HAZMAT team will implement their incident command system to manage the emergency response.
Calgren employees will only respond to incidental spills/releases within the immediate spill or release area (if it is safe to do so) and if the incident escalates, will evacuate and initiate the 911 emergency system "simultaneously".

Response procedures will involve isolating the area and evacuating all nonessential employees. A hazard assessment will be conducted, in order to determine the resources needed. Ammonia release will be controlled, contained, or confined by the local or regional HAZMAT teams to prevent further damage or injury. The responding team will critique the emergency respons
e upon completing response procedures. The response team commander(s) will facilitate the critique session.
